name: Proving how neural networks learn
gist: Theoretical analysis of deep learning through mechanisms like implicit bias, gradient descent convergence, and the internal structure of learned representations.
explain: Neural networks are the dominant model in machine learning, yet their theoretical foundations are surprisingly shaky. When you train a neural network by adjusting its weights using gradient descent — a simple algorithm that repeatedly moves in the direction that reduces error — it somehow finds weights that generalize. But why? The network has millions or billions of weights, thousands of possible local optima, and an enormous space of possible solutions. Gradient descent should get stuck, yet it often finds good solutions. This subtheme asks: what actually happens inside a neural network during training, and why does this process lead to good predictions?

The challenge is that neural networks are nonconvex — they have many hills and valleys in the space of possible solutions, not one single optimal point. Standard optimization theory cannot guarantee gradient descent will find a global optimum. Yet empirically, networks trained on random data often find terrible solutions (high error), while networks trained on real data find good solutions (low error). This suggests something about the structure of real data guides learning. Additionally, the sheer overparameterization — networks often have more weights than training examples — should lead to overfitting, yet somehow regularization (techniques that penalize complexity) and the structure of gradient descent itself prevent it.

Researchers prove statements about how gradient descent updates the network's internal representations, showing that it implicitly biases toward simple or smooth solutions. They study implicit regularization — the way an algorithm's mechanics (not explicit penalties) naturally avoid overfitting. They analyze how the network's early layers learn low-level features (edges, textures) and deeper layers combine them into high-level concepts (objects, animals). They examine specific architectures like convolutional neural networks (which exploit spatial structure in images) to understand why these designs work. The work also includes characterizing which functions a network can represent (expressivity) and which functions a given training algorithm can find (learnability), closing the gap between what is theoretically possible and what is practically learnable.

papers.title: Closed-form $\ell_r$ norm scaling with data for overparameterized linear regression and diagonal linear networks under $\ell_p$ bias
papers.contribution: The unified solution characterizes all ℓr norm scaling for r ∈ [1,p] under ℓp-biased interpolation and predicts which norms plateau versus grow with sample size.

papers.title: Continuum Transformers Perform In-Context Learning by Operator Gradient Descent
papers.contribution: Proves the operator learned in context is the Bayes Optimal Predictor in the infinite depth limit and provides empirical validations of this optimality result.

papers.title: Convergence Analysis of Tsetlin Machines under Noise-Free and Noisy Training Conditions: from $2$ Bits to $k$ Bits
papers.contribution: Provides robust theoretical foundation showing TM converges almost surely under noise-free training and that mislabeled samples permit efficient learning while irrelevant variables do not prevent convergence.

papers.title: Directional Convergence, Benign Overfitting of Gradient Descent in leaky ReLU two-layer Neural Networks
papers.contribution: Proves benign overfitting occurs on mixture data setting broader than prior nearly-orthogonal settings; identifies phase transition and characterizes cases where benign overfitting provably fails despite directional convergence.

papers.title: Neural Networks Learn Generic Multi-Index Models Near Information-Theoretic Limit
papers.contribution: Demonstrates sample and time complexity align with information-theoretic limits up to leading order, proving optimality and that optimal results require first-layer training beyond O(1) steps.

papers.title: No Prior, No Leakage: Revisiting Reconstruction Attacks in Trained Neural Networks
papers.contribution: Shows networks trained more extensively with stronger implicit bias are less susceptible to reconstruction attacks, reconciling privacy with generalization.

papers.title: On learning linear dynamical systems in context with attention layers
papers.contribution: Adds to understanding of transformer expressivity as in-context learners and offers plausible hypotheses for observations where they compete with Kalman filters in LDS settings.

papers.title: On the Convergence Behavior of Preconditioned Gradient Descent Toward the Rich Learning Regime
papers.contribution: They provide evidence that grokking represents a transitional behavior between the lazy NTK regime and the rich regime, demonstrating how PGD reduces these transition delays.

papers.title: On the Interpolation Effect of Score Smoothing in Diffusion Models
papers.contribution: Demonstrate smoothed score functions lead to interpolation within subspace while avoiding memorization, providing evidence that regularized neural networks induce similar smoothing effects.

papers.title: Rethinking Consistent Multi-Label Classification under Inexact Supervision
papers.contribution: The approach proves consistency with respect to two widely used multi-label classification metrics and derives convergence rates for estimation errors.

papers.title: Saddle-to-Saddle Dynamics Explains A Simplicity Bias Across Neural Network Architectures
papers.contribution: Shows neural networks learn increasingly complex solutions via iterative evolution near invariant manifolds and saddle-to-saddle transitions, unifying simplicity bias explanation.

papers.title: $\mathbf{Li_2}$: A Framework on Dynamics of Feature Emergence and Delayed Generalization
papers.contribution: The framework provides theoretical analysis of emerging features, their generalization properties, and the influence of hyperparameters on grokking behavior in 2-layer nonlinear networks.

papers.title: (Doubly) Exponential Lower Bounds for Follow the Regularized Leader in Potential Games
papers.contribution: Shows fictitious play takes doubly exponential time in multi-player games while establishing tight bounds for FTRL convergence dynamics.

papers.title: A Derandomization Framework for Structure Discovery: Applications in Neural Networks and Beyond
papers.contribution: The framework demonstrates structure discovery under weaker assumptions than prior work, including arbitrary network size and depth, with all parameters trainable and trained by any method achieving second-order stationary points.

papers.title: A Sharp KL-Convergence Analysis for Diffusion Models under Minimal Assumptions
papers.contribution: Proves convergence requiring O-tilde(d log^3/2(1/delta) / epsilon) steps with linear dependence on d, improving accuracy dependence while maintaining dimension scaling.

papers.title: A Theoretical Analysis of Mamba’s Training Dynamics: Filtering Relevant Features for Generalization in State Space Models
papers.contribution: Proves non-asymptotic sample complexity and convergence rate bounds; shows gating vectors align with class-relevant features via selective recurrence, formalizing a feature-selection mechanism.

papers.title: A Theory of How Pretraining Shapes Inductive Bias in Fine-Tuning
papers.contribution: Shows smaller initialization in early layers enables feature reuse and refinement, validated on ResNets and Transformers.

papers.title: A unified theory of feature learning in RNNs and DNNs
papers.contribution: Shows phase transition where learning signal overcomes weight noise, above which only RNNs develop correlated representations across timesteps, identifies inductive bias from weight sharing aiding generalization.

papers.title: Asymptotic analysis of shallow and deep forgetting in replay with neural collapse
papers.contribution: Shows replay asymmetrically affects forgetting levels, with minimal buffers preventing deep forgetting but substantial buffers needed for shallow forgetting, suggesting explicit Neural Collapse correction could improve efficiency.

papers.title: Attention's forward pass and Frank-Wolfe
papers.contribution: Proves sublinear convergence under negative semidefinite key-query matrices and exponential convergence with Voronoi structure under positive semidefinite case; establishes hardmax accuracy over exponentially long horizons.

papers.title: Breaking the Reversal Curse in Autoregressive Language Models via Identity Bridge
papers.contribution: Under Identity Bridge recipe, 1B model achieves 50% success on reversal tasks vs near-zero baseline, with theoretical proof that one-layer transformer breaks reversal curse under implicit bias.

papers.title: Conservation Laws for Modern Neural Architectures
papers.contribution: Identifies conservation invariants across modern architectures with experiments validating predicted invariants.

papers.title: Deep Networks Learn Deep Hierarchical Models
papers.contribution: Reaches the depth limit of efficient learnability with models requiring polynomial depth to express.

papers.title: Dichotomy of Feature Learning and Unlearning: Fast-Slow Analysis on Neural Networks with Stochastic Gradient Descent
papers.contribution: The analysis reveals that the strength of primary nonlinear terms in data induces feature unlearning while initial second-layer weight scales can mitigate it, with validated scaling laws and insights grounded in tensor programs and singular perturbation theory

papers.title: Diffusion Flow Matching: Dimension-Improved KL Bounds and Wasserstein Guarantees
papers.contribution: Derives state-of-the-art scaling in KL convergence bounds and extends analysis to 2-Wasserstein distance with consistent dimensional dependence.

papers.title: Efficient and Minimax Optimal In-context Nonparametric Regression with Transformers
papers.contribution: Shows transformers can efficiently approximate local polynomial estimators for Hölder-smooth nonparametric regression with substantially fewer parameters and pretraining sequences than prior results.

papers.title: Explaining Grokking and Information Bottleneck through Neural Collapse Emergence
papers.contribution: Validates theoretical findings on multiple datasets and architectures, explaining late-phase phenomena through neural collapse dynamics.

papers.title: Finite-Width Neural Tangent Kernels from Feynman Diagrams
papers.contribution: Extends stability results to finite-width NTKs and proves scale-invariant nonlinearities lack diagonal corrections, numerically validated for widths ≥20.

papers.title: Finite-time Convergence Analysis of Actor-Critic with Evolving Reward
papers.contribution: An O(1/√T) convergence rate is achievable when reward parameters evolve slowly, matching the best-known rate for static rewards.

papers.title: Flat Minima and Generalization: Insights from Stochastic Convex Optimization
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that flat empirical minima can incur trivial Ω(1) population risk while sharp minima generalize optimally, establishing population risk bounds for sharpness-aware algorithms using stability techniques.

papers.title: Full-Batch Gradient Descent Outperforms One-Pass SGD: Sample Complexity Separation in Single-Index Learning
papers.contribution: Shows full-batch GD outperforms one-pass SGD with n≥d samples and log d gradient steps for strong recovery, separating sample complexity by a log d factor.

papers.title: Generalization Below the Edge of Stability: The Role of Data Geometry
papers.contribution: For data on low-dimensional balls, generalization bounds adapt to intrinsic dimension; for isotropic distributions, mass concentration toward the sphere leads to memorization while dispersed mass enables learning shared patterns.

papers.title: Gradient Descent Dynamics of Rank-One Matrix Denoising
papers.contribution: We prove almost sure convergence as signal dimensions increase to infinity and show asymptotic behavior aligns with the Baik-Ben Arous-Péché phase transition.

papers.title: Gradient Descent as a Perceptron Algorithm: Understanding Dynamics and Implicit Acceleration
papers.contribution: Demonstrates nonlinearity in two-layer models yields faster iteration complexity Õ(√d) versus Ω(d) for linear models, helping explain implicit acceleration.

papers.title: Gradient Descent with Large Step Size Restores Symmetry in Deep Linear Networks with Multi-Pathway
papers.contribution: Clarifies how depth shapes pathway competition and explains why large-step GD favors shared representations over persistent single-pathway dominance.

papers.title: Gradient Flow Dynamics and Implicit Bias of Diagonal Linear Networks under Infinitesimal Initialization
papers.contribution: Establishes implicit bias corresponds to modified l1 norm; identifies Structural Invariant Manifold as key geometric structure shaping learning.

papers.title: Hard labels sampled from sparse targets mislead rotation invariant algorithms
papers.contribution: Demonstrates fundamental separation between rotation-invariant and non-rotation-invariant algorithms for sparse target learning in logistic regression.

papers.title: Implicit bias produces neural scaling laws in learning curves, from perceptrons to deep networks
papers.contribution: Novel dynamical scaling laws recover well-known asymptotic scaling and hold across CNNs, ResNets, and Vision Transformers.

papers.title: Inference-time Alignment with Rewards in Besov Spaces: Provable Advantages of Feature Learning and Multi-Step Policy Updates
papers.contribution: Shows feature learning capability of neural networks is crucial for improving performance, with multi-step algorithms improving regret especially under local structure.

papers.title: Interactive Learning of Single-Index Models via Stochastic Gradient Descent
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that SGD simultaneously achieves near-optimal sample complexity and regret guarantees across both phases for a broad class of link functions.

papers.title: Learning High-Dimensional Parity Functions with Product Networks using Gradient Descent
papers.contribution: Demonstrates convergence guarantees and polynomial complexity scaling laws validated on dimensions up to N = 100,000 with optimal hyperparameter choices.

papers.title: Learning to Execute Graph Algorithms Exactly with Graph Neural Networks
papers.contribution: Establishes rigorous learnability results for LOCAL model of distributed computation and demonstrates positive learnability for message flooding, BFS, DFS, and Bellman-Ford algorithms.

papers.title: Learning under Quantization for High-Dimensional Linear Regression
papers.contribution: The analysis distinguishes additive quantization effects (noise suppression scaled by batch size) from multiplicative quantization (spectral structure preservation).

papers.title: Neural Collapse in Multi-Task Learning
papers.contribution: Reveals that shared features form from scaled sums of task-specific weight vectors and uncovers inductive biases promoting task-specific feature alignment.

papers.title: Non-Stationary Online Structured Prediction with Surrogate Losses
papers.contribution: Upper bound depends on F_T and P_T (path length) with tight dependence; Polyak-style learning rate systematically yields target-loss bounds.

papers.title: ON THE ROLE OF IMPLICIT REGULARIZATION OF STOCHASTIC GRADIENT DESCENT IN GROUP ROBUSTNESS
papers.contribution: Theoretically establishes the phenomenon in linear models and empirically demonstrates SGD systematically suppresses spurious feature dependence across multiple deep neural network benchmarks.

papers.title: On the Convergence Rate of LoRA Gradient Descent
papers.contribution: LoRA gradient descent converges to stationary point at rate O(1/log T) without Lipschitz smoothness assumptions, reflecting actual practice.

papers.title: On the Convergence of Two-Layer Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with First-Layer Training
papers.contribution: Guarantees convergence to global minimum with m=O(n^2) hidden layer width, a significant O(n^6) polynomial improvement over two-layer ReLU networks.

papers.title: Outcome-Aware Spectral Feature Learning for Instrumental Variable Regression
papers.contribution: Maintains effectiveness under spectral misalignment through task-specific feature learning.

papers.title: Over-Alignment vs Over-Fitting: The Role of Feature Learning Strength in Generalization
papers.contribution: Establishes existence of optimal feature learning strength counter to prevailing intuition, showing large FLS induces over-alignment degrading generalization while small FLS leads to over-fitting.

papers.title: PCA of Probability Measures: Sparse and Dense Sampling Regimes
papers.contribution: Establishes convergence rates of n^(-1/2) + m^(-α) and proves the dense-regime rate is minimax optimal for the empirical covariance error, revealing sparse to dense transition in convergence behavior.

papers.title: Polynomial Convergence of Riemannian Diffusion Models
papers.contribution: Enables sharper analysis of diffusion models on non-Euclidean spaces with polynomially-sized steps.

papers.title: Preconditioning Neural Tangent Kernel for Adaptive Optimization
papers.contribution: Shows effectiveness of OAK method across architectures and justifies when/why kernel regime fails during finetuning.

papers.title: Preserving Plasticity in Continual Learning via Dynamical Isometry
papers.contribution: Consistently matches or outperforms existing approaches on supervised and RL continual-learning benchmarks designed to induce plasticity loss.

papers.title: Pruning at Initialisation through the lens of Graphon Limit: Convergence, Expressivity, and Generalisation
papers.contribution: Derives universal approximation theorem for sparse networks and connects limiting graphons to NTK-style generalization bounds with path-density interpretation.

papers.title: Richer Bayesian Last Layers with Subsampled NTK Features
papers.contribution: The method yields posterior variances provably greater than standard BLLs, improving calibration and uncertainty estimates on regression, bandits, and OOD detection with reduced computational cost.

papers.title: Saddle-To-Saddle Dynamics in Deep ReLU Networks: Low-Rank Bias in the First Saddle Escape
papers.contribution: Reveals that deep ReLU networks exhibit saddle-to-saddle dynamics with GD visiting a sequence of saddles with increasing bottleneck rank.

papers.title: Scaling Laws and Spectra of Shallow Neural Networks in the Feature Learning Regime
papers.contribution: Establishes precise link between scaling regimes and weight spectrum properties, validating empirical observations of power-law tails in weight spectrum correlating with generalization.

papers.title: Sharp asymptotic theory for Q-learning with \texttt{LD2Z} learning rate and its generalization
papers.contribution: We establish that LD2Z and PD2Z-ν achieve best-of-both-worlds: rapid decay from initialization and minimal asymptotic bias via sharp asymptotic theory.

papers.title: Spectral Reach: Understanding Neural Scaling as Progress into the Spectral Tail
papers.contribution: Shows larger models achieve lower losses by reaching further into the spectral tail, with feature learning enabling this through gradient amplification.

papers.title: Stop Guessing: Choosing the Optimization-Consistent Uncertainty Measurement for Evidential Deep Learning
papers.contribution: In this paper, we revisit EDL through the lens of optimization and establish a non-trivial connection: minimizing the expected cross-entropy loss over the Dirichlet prior implicitly encourages solutions akin to multi-class Support Vector Machines, maximizing d

papers.title: The Devil is in the Condition Numbers: Why is GLU Better than non-GLU Structure?
papers.contribution: Analysis reveals GLU's benefit lies primarily in accelerating optimization through improved conditioning rather than reducing generalization gap, with characteristic loss-crossing observed during training.

papers.title: The Implicit Bias of Depth: From Neural Collapse to Softmax Codes
papers.contribution: Provides first asymptotic and dynamic characterization showing depth drives low-rank alternatives to neural collapse corresponding to softmax codes.

papers.title: The Implicit Bias of Steepest Descent with Mini-batch Stochastic Gradient
papers.contribution: Shows momentum enables small-batch convergence to max-margin solutions and variance reduction recovers exact full-batch bias with explicit dimension-free convergence rates.

papers.title: Transfer Learning in Infinite Width Feature Learning Networks
papers.contribution: Provides interpretable conclusions on transfer performance depending on data regimes, task alignment, and feature learning strength, validated on linear/polynomial regression and real datasets.

papers.title: Transformers Can Learn Posterior Predictive Distributions In-Context
papers.contribution: Establishes error bounds for approximated PPD and demonstrates key role of normalization and attention depth in extrapolation capabilities.

papers.title: Transformers Learn the Optimal DDPM Denoiser for Multi-Token GMMs
papers.contribution: Quantifies required tokens per data point and training iterations for global convergence toward Bayes optimal risk of the denoising objective.

papers.title: Two-Layer Linear Auto-Regressive Models Estimate Latent States
papers.contribution: Demonstrates learned hidden representations coincide with Kalman filter state estimates up to similarity transformation, with theoretical convergence guarantees.

papers.title: UNDERSTANDING TRANSFORMERS FOR TIME SEIRES FORECASTING: A CASE STUDY ON MOIRAI
papers.contribution: Establishes learning bounds for pretraining under Dobrushin's condition; theoretical findings validate MOIRAI's design and explain empirical success in time series forecasting.

papers.title: Unifying Low Dimensional Spectra in Deep Learning
papers.contribution: Provides unifying analytic explanation for wide range of spectral phenomena in deep learning, including detailed eigenvector analysis beyond empirical eigenvalue characterizations, validated on both linear/ReLU networks and standard architectures.

papers.title: Why Deep Jacobian Spectra Separate: Depth-Induced Scaling and Singular-Vector Alignment
papers.contribution: Shows singular-value dynamics decouple under sufficient separation, mirroring balanced deep-linear analyses and mechanistically explaining implicit bias.
